$$\Bigl|\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}=\tfrac12\bigl(\partial_c\partial_a h^{c}{}_{b}+\partial_c\partial_b h^{c}{}_{a}-\Box h_{ab}-\partial_a\partial_b h\bigr).$$

**(c) Scalar curvature and Einstein tensor.** With the same constants,

$$\Bigl|S(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,S^{(1)}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad S^{(1)}=\partial_a\partial_bh^{ab}-\Box h,$$

and

$$\Bigl|G_{ab}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,G^{(1)}_{ab}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}=-\tfrac12\,\Box\bar h_{ab}+\partial^c\partial_{(a}\bar h_{b)c}-\tfrac12\,\eta_{ab}\,\partial^c\partial^d\bar h_{cd}.$$

**(d) Gauge transformation.** For every smooth covector field $\xi$ on
$\Omega$,

$$\bar h'{}_{ab}=\bar h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a+\eta_{ab}\,\partial^c\xi_c,\qquad \partial^a\bar h'{}_{ab}=\partial^a\bar h_{ab}-\Box\xi_b .$$

Consequently $h'$ is in harmonic gauge exactly when
$\Box\xi_b=\partial^a\bar h_{ab}$, and in that case

$$G^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=-\tfrac12\,\Box\bar h'{}_{ab}.$$

**(e) Gauge invariance of the first-order curvature.** For every smooth
covector field $\xi$ on $\Omega$,

$$\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(h),\qquad S^{(1)}(h')=S^{(1)}(h),\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=G^{(1)}_{ab}(h).$$

That is, subtracting the pure-gauge perturbation
$\partial_a\xi_b+\partial_b\xi_a$ from the first-order perturbation leaves
the first-order Ricci, scalar and Einstein tensors unchanged; their
first-order coefficients depend on $h$ only through its gauge-equivalence
class.

**(f) Quadratic remainder.** For every compact $K\subseteq\Omega$ there are
$\delta_0>0$ and $C_K<\infty$ such that for every smooth symmetric component
field $A=(A_{ab})$ on a neighborhood of $K$ with

$$B_K(A):=\sup_K\max_{a,b}|A_{ab}|+L\sup_K\max_{a,b,c}|\partial_cA_{ab}|+L^2\sup_K\max_{a,b,c,d}|\partial_c\partial_dA_{ab}|\le\delta_0,$$

the metric $\eta+A$ is Lorentzian of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $K$ and

$$\Bigl|G_{ab}(\eta+A)(p)-G^{(1)}_{ab}(A)(p)\Bigr|\le \frac{C_K\,B_K(A)^2}{L^2}\qquad(p\in K),$$

where $G^{(1)}_{ab}(A)$ is the right-hand side of the displayed formula of
(c) with $h$ replaced by $A$, and $G_{ab}(\eta+A)$ is the Einstein tensor of
the metric with components $\eta_{ab}+A_{ab}$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with inertial chart $x$ and
constant metric components $\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and let
$\Omega\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set, identified with its image under
$x$; all components below are taken in the inertial chart. Let $c>0$ be a
real parameter.

**(a) Flat linearized family.** A **flat linearized family over $\Omega$**
consists of a number $\varepsilon_1>0$, a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $h$ on $\Omega$ with components $h_{ab}$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) — the **first-order
perturbation** — and a smooth family $q$ of symmetric component fields
$q_{ab}(\lambda,p)$, defined for $\lambda\in(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)$
and $p\in\Omega$, such that for every $\lambda$ with
$0<|\lambda|<\varepsilon_1$ the component field

$$g_{ab}(\lambda,p):=\eta_{ab}+\lambda\,h_{ab}(p)+\lambda^2\,q_{ab}(\lambda,p)$$

is the component field of a smooth Lorentzian metric $g(\lambda)$ on
$\Omega$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $q$ is the **normalized remainder**. The
family is thus normalized so that $g(0)=\eta$ is its value at
$\lambda=0$ and $h=\partial_\lambda g(\lambda)|_{\lambda=0}$. No assumption
is made that $g(\lambda)$ solves any field equation; the metrics $g(\lambda)$
are the mathematical input of the linearization.

**(b) First-order coefficients.** Let $A(\lambda)$ stand for any of the
component families $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(g(\lambda))$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g(\lambda))$, $S(g(\lambda))$,
$G_{ab}(g(\lambda))$ of the metric-selected connection of $g(\lambda)$; these
are smooth in $(\lambda,p)$ because the Christoffel symbols, the curvature
components and the inverse metric are smooth functions of the metric
components and their derivatives
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Define the **first-order
coefficients**

$$\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}:=\partial_\lambda\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},\quad \operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}:=\partial_\lambda\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},$$
$$S^{(1)}:=\partial_\lambda S(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}:=\partial_\lambda G_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0}.$$

**(c) Index conventions.** Indices on first-order quantities are raised and
lowered with the flat metric $\eta$ and its inverse $\eta^{ab}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]): $\partial^a:=\eta^{ab}\partial_b$,
$h^{ab}:=\eta^{ac}\eta^{bd}h_{cd}$, and

$$\Box:=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b=-\partial_0^2+\partial_1^2+\partial_2^2+\partial_3^2$$

is the **d'Alembertian** of the flat metric, applied componentwise to
component families. The **trace** of $h$ and the **trace-reversed
perturbation** are

$$h:=\eta^{ab}h_{ab},\qquad \bar h_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\tfrac12\,h\,\eta_{ab} .$$

The inverse passage is the same formula, $\bar h_{ab}$'s trace being
$\eta^{ab}\bar h_{ab}=h-2h=-h$: explicitly

$$h_{ab}=\bar h_{ab}-\tfrac12\,\eta_{ab}\,\eta^{cd}\bar h_{cd} .$$

**(d) Gauge transformation.** For a smooth covector field $\xi_b$ on
$\Omega$ define the **gauge-transformed first-order perturbation**

$$h'_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a .$$

This is the first-order perturbation of the pullback family
$\Phi_{-\lambda}^*g(\lambda)$ along the local flows $\Phi_s$ of the vector
field $\xi^a=\eta^{ab}\xi_b$, that is, the perturbation produced by the
infinitesimal chart change $x'^a=x^a+\lambda\xi^a$ and re-read on the fixed
inertial chart; the transformation of the metric components displayed here
is the linearization of the Jacobian transformation law, and
its consequences for $\bar h$ and for $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}$, $S^{(1)}$
and $G^{(1)}$ are proved separately on this page (the first-order curvature
and gauge theorem that follows this definition).
The perturbation $h$ is **in harmonic gauge** (also called de Donder gauge)
when

$$\partial^a\bar h_{ab}=0 .$$

**(e) Scope.** This item fixes the objects of the flat linearization: the
normalized family, the first-order coefficients defined as exact
$\lambda$-derivatives, the trace reversal, the d'Alembertian and the gauge
transformation. It asserts no explicit formula for the first-order
coefficients, no existence of a gauge representative satisfying (d), no
solution of any linearized field equation and no physical interpretation;
those are separate results. The notation is tied to the inertial chart: a
change of chart is a different operation from the gauge transformation (d),
which changes the metric family inside the fixed chart.

derivations.claim: (Differentiating the curvature formula.) By [L2] the Christoffel component families are smooth in $(\lambda,p)$ with $\Gamma(0)=0$. Differentiating the coordinate formula of [L1] in $\lambda$ at $0$, the product terms $\Gamma\Gamma$ contribute $2\Gamma(0)\partial_\lambda\Gamma(0)=0$, so $R^{(1)a}{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{cb}$; this also shows that the coefficient is defined as the derivative of a differentiable component family. Substituting the formula of [L2] into $\eta_{ae}R^{(1)e}{}_{bcd}$ and using $\eta_{ae}\Gamma^{(1)e}{}_{db}=\Gamma^{(1)}_{adb}=\tfrac12(\partial_dh_{ab}+\partial_bh_{ad}-\partial_ah_{db})$ gives $$R^{(1)}_{abcd}=\tfrac12\partial_c(\partial_dh_{ab}+\partial_bh_{ad}-\partial_ah_{db})-\tfrac12\partial_d(\partial_ch_{ab}+\partial_bh_{ac}-\partial_ah_{cb}),$$ and the two terms $+\tfrac12\partial_c\partial_dh_{ab}$ and $-\tfrac12\partial_d\partial_ch_{ab}$ cancel by [L3], leaving the displayed formula. This proves (a).

(Gauge invariance.) Let $H_{ab}:=\partial_a\xi_b+\partial_b\xi_a$, so that $h'=h-H$ and $R^{(1)}(h')=R^{(1)}(h)-R^{(1)}(H)$ by [L6]. By the formula of step 1.1, $$R^{(1)}_{abcd}(H)=\tfrac12\bigl(\partial_b\partial_cH_{ad}+\partial_a\partial_dH_{bc}-\partial_a\partial_cH_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dH_{ac}\bigr).$$ Substituting $H_{ad}=\partial_a\xi_d+\partial_d\xi_a$ and expanding, the eight third-derivative terms group as $$(\partial_b\partial_c\partial_a\xi_d-\partial_a\partial_c\partial_b\xi_d)+(\partial_b\partial_c\partial_d\xi_a-\partial_b\partial_d\partial_c\xi_a)+(\partial_a\partial_d\partial_b\xi_c-\partial_b\partial_d\partial_a\xi_c)+(\partial_a\partial_d\partial_c\xi_b-\partial_a\partial_c\partial_d\xi_b),$$ and each parenthesis vanishes by [L3]. Hence $R^{(1)}(H)=0$ and $R^{(1)}(h')=R^{(1)}(h)$. This proves (b).

(Planar waves.) Let $h_{ab}=F_{ab}(u)$; by [L4], $\partial_b\partial_ch_{ad}=F''_{ad}n_bn_c$, and substituting into the formula of step 1.1 gives the displayed planar formula. If $F_{0a}=0$, then substituting $n_0=1$, $n_i=0$ for $i=1,2$ and $n_3=-1$ gives $R^{(1)}_{0i0j}=\tfrac12(n_in_0F''_{0j}+n_0n_jF''_{i0}-n_0n_0F''_{ij}-n_in_jF''_{00})=-\tfrac12F''_{ij}$. For the raised component, the four-term formula of step 1.1 is antisymmetric in the first and in the last index pair, so $R^{(1)}_{a00j}=-R^{(1)}_{a0j0}=R^{(1)}_{0aj0}=-R^{(1)}_{0a0j}=-\bigl(-\tfrac12F''_{aj}\bigr)=\tfrac12F''_{aj}$; raising the first index gives $R^{(1)i}{}_{00j}=\eta^{ia}\tfrac12F''_{aj}=+\tfrac12F''{}^i{}_j$. If in addition the profile is TT, then $F''_{ij}$ vanishes whenever $i=j=3$ or one index equals $3$, and $F''_{11}=-F''_{22}=A_+''$, $F''_{12}=F''_{21}=A_\times''$; the displayed components follow. This proves (c).

(Ricci contraction.) Contracting the formula of step 1.1 with $\eta^{ac}$ term by term gives $$\eta^{ac}R^{(1)}_{abcd}=\tfrac12\bigl(\partial_b\partial_ch^c{}_d+\partial_a\partial_dh^{a}{}_b-\Box h_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dh\bigr),$$ which is the formula of [L6] for $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{bd}$ (the first two terms are the same contraction with renamed dummy indices). For a TT planar perturbation, [L4] gives zero trace, zero divergence and $\Box h_{bd}=0$, so every term in the Ricci formula of [L6] vanishes, independently of boundedness of the profiles. Thus $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{bd}=0$ and its contraction $S^{(1)}=0$ by [L1]. This proves (d).

(Conclusion.) Steps 1.1, 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3 prove the four clauses from the coordinate curvature formula, the first-order Christoffel symbols and the commutation of partial derivatives. No field equation or profile boundedness is assumed: the vanishing statement of (d) follows directly from the null-phase and TT identities; no choice principle beyond the inherited countable choice of the cited suppliers is used.

boundaries.evidence: The family parameter belongs to (-epsilon_1,epsilon_1) with epsilon_1>0, so lambda=0 is available for the curvature derivative in step 1.1. The flat-linearized-family definition requires nonempty Omega; the finite component sums have four indices, and no sum over arbitrary families is taken.

step 1.1: the first-order coefficients are linear in the perturbation and its derivatives, so the zero perturbation has vanishing first-order curvature; clause (d) and step 2.3 include the zero case Ric^{(1)} = 0 for a TT planar perturbation.

boundaries.reason: The coefficient is defined as a derivative at lambda = 0 and no unit scalar, rank-one case or single-parameter normalization is singled out; the length scale epsilon_1 is arbitrary.

boundaries.evidence: statement: the family is a flat linearized family, so its metrics are Lorentzian for |lambda| < epsilon_1 and the inverse metric used in the curvature formula exists; step 1.1 differentiates at lambda = 0 where the metric is eta, so no degenerate metric occurs.

boundaries.reason: All claims are pointwise identities on the open set Omega and one parameter derivative at the interior point lambda = 0; no boundary point of Omega or endpoint of the parameter interval is used.

boundaries.evidence: statement clause (b) applies to an arbitrary but fixed smooth covector field xi, a single object and not a selection; the proof chooses no family, and the inherited countable choice of the cited suppliers is the only choice principle involved.

boundaries.reason: The theorem states equalities and invariance, not an equivalence.

Clauses (a)-(d) give a first-derivative curvature formula, gauge invariance, planar components and a Ricci contraction. In particular clause (b) never concludes that equal curvature implies a pure gauge difference, and step 2.1 proves only invariance.

risk_review.notes: All five steps checked against the exact curvature convention, first-order Christoffel and mixed-partial suppliers. Differentiation removes Gamma products; eight gauge third-derivative terms cancel. R0101=-Aplus-double-prime/2 and R^i_00j=+F-double-prime/2 have the stated signs; eta contraction recovers Ricci. Amended L1 to distinguish exact g-contractions from eta-contractions of first-order coefficients. Original proof of TT Ricci=0 invoked the bounded-profile TT solutions result for unrestricted profiles; repaired by applying the zero-trace/divergence/Box identities directly to Ricci formula, preserving the richer arbitrary smooth-profile statement. Null lemma orientation repair does not affect derivative uses. Risk review complete; no empirical inference.

citations.quote:
Adopt as the field law of the direct-equation presentation of the classical
gravitational framework, for models satisfying
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], the following statement.

**(i) The equation.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab}$ be the Einstein tensor of that
connection ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Let
$T$ be the model's stress-energy tensor field on its matter domain
$U\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]) and let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be a constant parameter with dimension
$\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $G_N>0$, $c>0$ the constants of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Adopt

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}\,T_{ab}\qquad\text{on }U$$

as the field law of the model. Writing
$\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ and $T_{ab}=g_{ac}g_{bd}T^{cd}$ for the lowered tensor,
the equation reads $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$

**(ii) Matter content.** The equation constrains the metric and the matter of
the model jointly. A model specifies its matter sector as in
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]: a scalar-field model with its action
and stress-energy tensor ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), or a dust or perfect-fluid model with prescribed
stress-energy tensor and matter equations. The consistency condition that
every solution must satisfy, $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$, is not adopted separately; it
is a consequence of the equation and of the contracted second Bianchi identity
and is derived in [[pthm-gr-einstein-consistency-and-energy-conditions]].

**(iii) Alternative presentation.** The action formulation of the same field
law is adopted separately in [[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]]. A
model adopts exactly one of the two presentations. They are alternative
presentations of one classical field law: the action-to-equation theorem of
this page identifies the equation obtained from stationarity of the total
action with the equation displayed in clause (i), and the direct presentation
is not an additional premise of an action-formulated model.

**(iv) Status and scope.** The equation is an adopted law of the model. It is
not derived from mathematical symmetry, from the equivalence principle, or
from observation; covariance and correspondence arguments motivate but do not
prove it. No numerical value of $c$, $G_N$ or $\Lambda$ is asserted, and no
claim is made that any particular metric or matter configuration solves the
equation or describes nature. The smooth-branch exclusions of
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] apply: distributional or
lower-dimensional sources, boundaries with junction conditions, and non-smooth
fields are outside this formulation. Comparisons of a model's predictions with
data test the combined model — geometry, matter content and this law — and
agreement is evidence about that combination, not a proof of the postulate.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework the
following statements.

**(i) Spacetime model.** The spacetime of a model of the framework is a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ as in
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: a smooth four-manifold $M$ without
boundary, a Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), and a time orientation $N$. Its points represent
idealized physical events; the vector $N$ fixes which causal directions are
future-directed. At each event $p\in M$, every nonzero tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is
classified by the sign of $g_p(v,v)$ as in
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], and each nonzero causal vector is
future- or past-directed according to the sign of $g_p(v,N_p)$. The zero
vector is neither timelike, null, spacelike nor causal. This is a
pointwise rule and does not require choosing a curve through $p$. The metric
$g$ is the gravitational field of the model: it is the object that the field
law of the framework constrains, and the curvature $R^g$ of the uniquely constructed torsion-free
$g$-compatible connection $\nabla^g$ of
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] is the model's representation of
gravity. That supplier defines $R^g(X,Y)Z=\nabla^g_X\nabla^g_YZ-\nabla^g_Y\nabla^g_XZ-\nabla^g_{[X,Y]}Z$
and proves the connection exists; this clause adds no independent connection
field. The rules by which ideal clocks, test bodies and
light rays couple to $g$ are adopted separately as physical assumptions of the
framework.

**(ii) Classical domain.** Geometry and matter are treated as classical
continuum fields: the model describes macroscopic configurations of matter and
a classical metric, with no quantum description of either. The framework makes
no claim that a real spacetime is exactly such a manifold, that matter is
exactly a classical continuum, or that the smooth description applies to
arbitrarily small scales or arbitrarily strong fields; those are domain
limitations of the model family, not consequences of it.

**(iii) Unity of the model.** A model of the framework is specified by its
geometry $(M,g,N)$ together with its matter content and the field law adopted
for it; the geometry alone selects no matter configuration and no dynamics
(the matter assumptions are
adopted separately, in the companion postulate on matter content). Physical
parameters enter through
the unit conventions of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]; no
numerical value of a constant is asserted here.

**(iv) Smooth-branch restriction.** The fields of a model are defined on an
open domain of $M$; the metric is $C^\infty$ on all of $M$ and $M$ has no
boundary. Configurations in which a field fails to be smooth on a nonempty open
set, in which matter is concentrated on a lower-dimensional set in a way that
produces a distributional stress-energy tensor, or in which $M$ carries a
boundary, are outside the stated smooth domain of the framework and require
mathematics not supplied by these postulates.

**(v) Status.** These are adopted assumptions. They are not derived from the
mathematics of manifolds, from any symmetry principle, or from experiment; the
equivalence principle and covariance arguments motivate but do not prove them.
Testing the framework means comparing predictions computed from a fully
specified model — geometry, matter content and field law — with observations,
and agreement is evidence about the model, not a proof of these postulates.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework, in
addition to [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]], the following statements
about the matter content of a model.

**(i) Matter content is model input.** A model of the framework specifies its
nongravitational fields or matter and their explicit equations of motion and
couplings. The geometric data $(M,g,N)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and covariance of the model's equations
under relabelling of events do not select those fields, equations or couplings.
Here covariance means that, on overlapping smooth charts, the component
transformations specified for the model's fields carry solutions of the
equations in one chart to solutions of the same equations in the other.
Different matter specifications over the same geometry are different models of
the framework, and no dynamical selection principle is asserted.

**(ii) Smooth matter and its stress-energy tensor.** The matter of a model on
its matter domain is represented by smooth fields on an open domain
$U\subseteq M$, and the model's stress-energy tensor is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on $U$ of
[[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]], with the unit reading recorded there.
The relation of $T$ to the matter fields is part of the model: a model derived
from an action defines $T$ as the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of that action,
while a model that prescribes $T$ directly is a separate source model.

**(iii) Consistency with the field law.** Where a model prescribes $T$
independently of matter fields, the prescription is admissible only if it meets
the consistency conditions imposed by the gravitational field law adopted for
the model, stated where that law is stated. If a model specifies a real-valued
action functional on its admissible metric and matter configurations, the
action, its dependence on those fields, its stated symmetries, and the matter
equations obtained from it are part of the model. Any conservation identity
used for $T$ when those equations hold must be established from that model's
action, symmetries, equations, and regularity hypotheses; it is not assumed
for an arbitrary action or arbitrary smooth symmetric $T$.

**(iv) Energy conditions are optional additional assumptions.** A model may
adopt any of the pointwise inequalities of [[def-gr-energy-conditions]] as
further assumptions on its stress-energy tensor. The general framework
postulates impose none automatically. A particular matter model may imply one
or more of them; any such implication must be established from that model's
equations and hypotheses. Each model records which conditions, if any, it
adopts, and a model that adopts none is not thereby excluded.

**(v) Scope and exclusions.** Idealizations such as unmodeled self-force,
finite-size and tidal corrections, dispersion, dissipation, and quantum effects
are outside the framework unless the model's explicit equations include them;
matter concentrated in a distributional or lower-dimensional source, and
matter configurations whose fields fail to be smooth on the model domain, are
outside the stated smooth branch and require additional mathematics. The
adoption of a matter model is not a claim that it describes nature.

This item fixes the unit and coordinate readings of the explicitly defined
Lorentzian objects, smooth-curve proper time and four-velocity of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], the tensor fields of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and the constructed connection,
curvature, Ricci and scalar fields of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]].
It states conventions, not a physical law or a measurement.

**(a) Constants and tensor slot.** Adopt $c>0$ with SI dimension
$\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, $G_N>0$ with dimension
$\mathrm m^3\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm s^{-2}$, and a signed parameter
$\Lambda$ with dimension $\mathrm m^{-2}$. No numerical value is asserted.
Define $\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$, of dimension
$\mathrm m^{-1}\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm s^2$.
For a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor $T$ adopt the convention that its
components $T_{AB}=T(e_A,e_B)$ in an ordered $g$-orthonormal basis are energy
per volume, $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-1}\mathrm s^{-2}$.
This is a tensor slot and unit convention; interpreting a particular $T$ as
matter is a subsequent definition. Therefore $\kappa T_{AB}$ has dimension
$\mathrm m^{-2}$. No positivity, conservation or matter realization is assumed.

**(b) Coordinates and dimensions.** In a length-coordinate chart,
$x^0=ct$ and all four coordinates have units $\mathrm m$; $g_{ab}$ are
dimensionless and the quadratic line element $ds^2=g_{ab}dx^adx^b$ has units
$\mathrm m^2$. The Christoffel symbols defined by
$\nabla^g_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]) have units
$\mathrm m^{-1}$: the constructed formula differentiates dimensionless
$g_{ab}$ once with respect to a length coordinate. Curvature components have
units $\mathrm m^{-2}$ since the curvature operator differentiates the
connection once more and includes products of two connection coefficients;
so do $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ and scalar curvature $S$ in these coordinates.
In a time-coordinate chart $x^0=t$ has units $\mathrm s$, and $g_{00}$ has
units $\mathrm m^2\,\mathrm s^{-2}$; mixed, spatial, angular or other chart
components have the dimensions obtained by the coordinate Jacobians. A single
component has no universal dimension in a general chart. Orthonormal-frame
readings use the normalized geometric basis, with its length normalization.

**(c) Curves and invariant readings.** For the smooth future timelike curve
and positive scaling parameter of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] (e),
read $c$ as in (a) and
$\tau(s)=\tau_0+c^{-1}\int_{s_0}^{s}\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}\,dr$
as a proper-time parameter in seconds. Its four-velocity $U=d\gamma/d\tau$
has length-coordinate and normalized orthonormal components in
$\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$; in a time-coordinate chart $U^0=dt/d\tau$
is dimensionless and other component dimensions follow the coordinates.
Lorentzian length $c\,\Delta\tau$ is in metres. The tensors $R^g$,
$\operatorname{Ric}$ and the scalar $S$ have the orthonormal readings
$\mathrm m^{-2}$, whereas the lowered curvature components in a mixed chart
have the units required by the metric and coordinate slots.

**(d) Future observer readings and SI restoration.** Let $n$ be a future
unit timelike vector, $g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,N)<0$. Define
$\rho_n:=T(n,n)$, $j_n:=-\sharp(T(n,\cdot))$ and its spatial part
$\phi_n:=j_n-\rho_n n$; indeed $g(j_n,n)=-\rho_n$, so
$g(\phi_n,n)=0$. In a $g$-orthonormal basis with $e_0=n$, set
$\phi^i=-T(e_0,e_i)=T^{0i}$ for $i=1,2,3$. The **SI energy flux** vector
and **SI momentum density** covector are, respectively,

$$q_n:=c\phi_n,\qquad p_n:=\phi_n^{\flat}/c,\qquad q_n^i=-cT_{0i},\qquad (p_n)_i=-T_{0i}/c.$$

Thus $\rho_n$ and each $\phi^i$ have units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$;
$q_n^i$ has units $\mathrm W\,\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $(p_n)_i$ has units
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-2}\mathrm s^{-1}$. Stress components $T_{ij}$ have
units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}=\mathrm{Pa}$. Tensor components retain the
common energy-density units; the factors of $c$ convert their mixed readings
to different SI quantities. Future-directedness and the signs here are part
of the convention, not positivity assumptions on $T$.

**(e) Natural units.** Setting $c=1$, or additionally $G_N=1$, abbreviates
these dimensionful conventions. Restore the factors displayed above before
comparison with SI quantities; in particular the same spatial tensor component
corresponds to energy flux multiplied by $c$ and momentum density divided by
$c$. In a chart whose coordinates $x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3$ are all lengths and whose
metric components are $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, a nonzero null tangent
vector $v=(v^0,\mathbf v)$, null as in clause (b) of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], satisfies
$\|\mathbf v\|_2:=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}=|v^0|$. Since $v\ne0$, this
implies $v^0\ne0$, so $\|\mathbf v\|_2/|v^0|=1$. This is a coordinate identity
for the null condition, not a postulate about light propagation, and it does
not change the physical constant $c$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with inertial chart $x$ and
constant metric components $\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and let
$\Omega\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set, identified with its image under
$x$; all components below are taken in the inertial chart. Let $c>0$ be a
real parameter.

**(a) Flat linearized family.** A **flat linearized family over $\Omega$**
consists of a number $\varepsilon_1>0$, a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $h$ on $\Omega$ with components $h_{ab}$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) — the **first-order
perturbation** — and a smooth family $q$ of symmetric component fields
$q_{ab}(\lambda,p)$, defined for $\lambda\in(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)$
and $p\in\Omega$, such that for every $\lambda$ with
$0<|\lambda|<\varepsilon_1$ the component field

$$g_{ab}(\lambda,p):=\eta_{ab}+\lambda\,h_{ab}(p)+\lambda^2\,q_{ab}(\lambda,p)$$

is the component field of a smooth Lorentzian metric $g(\lambda)$ on
$\Omega$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $q$ is the **normalized remainder**. The
family is thus normalized so that $g(0)=\eta$ is its value at
$\lambda=0$ and $h=\partial_\lambda g(\lambda)|_{\lambda=0}$. No assumption
is made that $g(\lambda)$ solves any field equation; the metrics $g(\lambda)$
are the mathematical input of the linearization.

**(b) First-order coefficients.** Let $A(\lambda)$ stand for any of the
component families $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(g(\lambda))$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g(\lambda))$, $S(g(\lambda))$,
$G_{ab}(g(\lambda))$ of the metric-selected connection of $g(\lambda)$; these
are smooth in $(\lambda,p)$ because the Christoffel symbols, the curvature
components and the inverse metric are smooth functions of the metric
components and their derivatives
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Define the **first-order
coefficients**

$$\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}:=\partial_\lambda\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},\quad \operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}:=\partial_\lambda\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},$$
$$S^{(1)}:=\partial_\lambda S(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}:=\partial_\lambda G_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0}.$$

**(c) Index conventions.** Indices on first-order quantities are raised and
lowered with the flat metric $\eta$ and its inverse $\eta^{ab}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]): $\partial^a:=\eta^{ab}\partial_b$,
$h^{ab}:=\eta^{ac}\eta^{bd}h_{cd}$, and

$$\Box:=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b=-\partial_0^2+\partial_1^2+\partial_2^2+\partial_3^2$$

is the **d'Alembertian** of the flat metric, applied componentwise to
component families. The **trace** of $h$ and the **trace-reversed
perturbation** are

$$h:=\eta^{ab}h_{ab},\qquad \bar h_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\tfrac12\,h\,\eta_{ab} .$$

The inverse passage is the same formula, $\bar h_{ab}$'s trace being
$\eta^{ab}\bar h_{ab}=h-2h=-h$: explicitly

$$h_{ab}=\bar h_{ab}-\tfrac12\,\eta_{ab}\,\eta^{cd}\bar h_{cd} .$$

**(d) Gauge transformation.** For a smooth covector field $\xi_b$ on
$\Omega$ define the **gauge-transformed first-order perturbation**

$$h'_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a .$$

This is the first-order perturbation of the pullback family
$\Phi_{-\lambda}^*g(\lambda)$ along the local flows $\Phi_s$ of the vector
field $\xi^a=\eta^{ab}\xi_b$, that is, the perturbation produced by the
infinitesimal chart change $x'^a=x^a+\lambda\xi^a$ and re-read on the fixed
inertial chart; the transformation of the metric components displayed here
is the linearization of the Jacobian transformation law, and
its consequences for $\bar h$ and for $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}$, $S^{(1)}$
and $G^{(1)}$ are proved separately on this page (the first-order curvature
and gauge theorem that follows this definition).
The perturbation $h$ is **in harmonic gauge** (also called de Donder gauge)
when

$$\partial^a\bar h_{ab}=0 .$$

**(e) Scope.** This item fixes the objects of the flat linearization: the
normalized family, the first-order coefficients defined as exact
$\lambda$-derivatives, the trace reversal, the d'Alembertian and the gauge
transformation. It asserts no explicit formula for the first-order
coefficients, no existence of a gauge representative satisfying (d), no
solution of any linearized field equation and no physical interpretation;
those are separate results. The notation is tied to the inertial chart: a
change of chart is a different operation from the gauge transformation (d),
which changes the metric family inside the fixed chart.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.


**(d) Intrinsic construction before physical use.** For smooth local vector
fields define the Koszul expression

$$K(X,Y,Z):=Xg(Y,Z)+Yg(Z,X)-Zg(X,Y)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X).$$

Define $\nabla^g_XY$ by $2g(\nabla^g_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)$ for every smooth local
$Z$. The proof below establishes existence, smoothness, the affine-connection
rules, metric compatibility, torsion freedom and uniqueness; it uses symmetry
and nondegeneracy, not positive definiteness. Thus $\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$
has this unique element, called the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$. The later
nondegenerate-metric theorem retains its fuller tensor-derivative statement.
Its Christoffel symbols in any chart are defined by
$\nabla^g_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]) and obey

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12 g^{ad}(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}),\qquad a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3.$$

**(e) Basic curvature and contractions.** The **curvature** of this connection
is the operator of [[def-curvature-of-an-affine-connection]], with the fixed
sign convention

$$R^g(X,Y)Z:=\nabla^g_X\nabla^g_YZ-\nabla^g_Y\nabla^g_XZ-\nabla^g_{[X,Y]}Z.$$

The general affine-connection theorem
[[thm-curvature-is-a-type-one-three-tensor]] proves that it depends pointwise
only on $X,Y,Z$ and is a smooth tensor. Define its chart components by
$R^g(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^a{}_{bcd}\partial_a$.
Define the **Ricci tensor** and **scalar curvature** pointwise by

$$\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,w):=\operatorname{tr}(z\mapsto R^g_p(z,w)v),\qquad S(p):=\operatorname{tr}(\sharp_p\circ\operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p),\qquad \operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p(v):=\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,\cdot).$$

Here $\sharp$ is the inverse metric isomorphism and traces are the
basis-independent trace of [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. Equivalently,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\sum_aR^a{}_{bad}$ and
$S=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}$, all sums from $0$ through $3$.
These are well-defined smooth fields by finite contraction of the smooth
components of $R^g$ and $g^{-1}$; basis independence follows from the trace
and the intrinsic maps just defined. No symmetry identity or field equation
is assumed here. Lowering the curvature output gives
$R_{abcd}=g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd}$, so the definitions agree with the full later
curvature item, which proves the remaining symmetries and coordinate formulas.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. That $R_{abcd}$ are the components of a smooth $(0,4)$-tensor
field and that $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth
symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field, so that the contractions above are
basis-independent and do not depend on the chart, is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clauses (a)-(d); the Ricci symmetry
is part of that statement.

Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth manifolds, let $F:M\to N$ be a map, let $p\in M$ and
let $r\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$, where $\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$.
For $m,q\in\mathbb N_0$ and an open set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, a map
$g:E\to\mathbb R^q$ is **of class $C^r$** as follows. When $m=0$, every such
map is declared $C^r$. When $m\ge1$, each component $g_l$ with $l<q$ must be
$C^r$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]; when $q=0$ this
component condition is vacuous.
Suppose $F$ is continuous at $p$. Then $F$ is **of class $C^r$ at $p$** when
there are smooth charts $(U,\varphi)$ of $M$ at $p$ and $(V,\psi)$ of $N$ at
$F(p)$ with $F(U)\subseteq V$ such that the coordinate representative

$$\psi\circ F\circ\varphi^{-1}:\varphi(U)\longrightarrow\psi(V)$$

([[def-coordinate-representation-of-a-map]]) is of class $C^r$ on a
neighbourhood of $\varphi(p)$ in this componentwise Euclidean sense. By
[[lem-chart-independence-of-c-r-smoothness]], this condition is independent of
the chosen charts: if one such representative is $C^r$, then every one is, so
"some charts" may be read as "any charts". A map is **$C^r$ on an open set**
$W\subseteq M$ when it is continuous on $W$ and $C^r$ at every point of $W$. A
map that is $C^r$ for every finite $r$ — equivalently $C^\infty$ — is called
**smooth**; the term **$C^r$ map between smooth manifolds** is reserved for the
case where $F$ is continuous and the representative condition holds at every
point of $M$.

Let $\Omega\subseteq M$ be an open set of the flat model
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]], let
$(\varepsilon_1,h,q)$ be a flat linearized family over $\Omega$ with
first-order coefficients $\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}$,
$\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}$, $S^{(1)}$, $G^{(1)}_{ab}$ and with trace
reversal $\bar h$, d'Alembertian $\Box$ and gauge transformation
$h'_{ab}=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a$ as in
[[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]], and let $L>0$ be a length scale.
All components are taken in the inertial chart and all contractions are
with $\eta$ and $\eta^{-1}$.

**(a) Christoffel symbols.** For every compact $K\subseteq\Omega$ there is a
constant $C_K<\infty$ such that for all $p\in K$ and
$0<|\lambda|\le\varepsilon_1/2$,

$$\Bigl|\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad \Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,\eta^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bh_{cd}+\partial_ch_{bd}-\partial_dh_{bc}\bigr).$$

**(b) Ricci tensor.** With the same constants (enlarged if necessary),

$$\Bigl|\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}=\tfrac12\bigl(\partial_c\partial_a h^{c}{}_{b}+\partial_c\partial_b h^{c}{}_{a}-\Box h_{ab}-\partial_a\partial_b h\bigr).$$

**(c) Scalar curvature and Einstein tensor.** With the same constants,

$$\Bigl|S(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,S^{(1)}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad S^{(1)}=\partial_a\partial_bh^{ab}-\Box h,$$

and

$$\Bigl|G_{ab}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,G^{(1)}_{ab}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}=-\tfrac12\,\Box\bar h_{ab}+\partial^c\partial_{(a}\bar h_{b)c}-\tfrac12\,\eta_{ab}\,\partial^c\partial^d\bar h_{cd}.$$

**(d) Gauge transformation.** For every smooth covector field $\xi$ on
$\Omega$,

$$\bar h'{}_{ab}=\bar h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a+\eta_{ab}\,\partial^c\xi_c,\qquad \partial^a\bar h'{}_{ab}=\partial^a\bar h_{ab}-\Box\xi_b .$$

Consequently $h'$ is in harmonic gauge exactly when
$\Box\xi_b=\partial^a\bar h_{ab}$, and in that case

$$G^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=-\tfrac12\,\Box\bar h'{}_{ab}.$$

**(e) Gauge invariance of the first-order curvature.** For every smooth
covector field $\xi$ on $\Omega$,

$$\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(h),\qquad S^{(1)}(h')=S^{(1)}(h),\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=G^{(1)}_{ab}(h).$$

That is, subtracting the pure-gauge perturbation
$\partial_a\xi_b+\partial_b\xi_a$ from the first-order perturbation leaves
the first-order Ricci, scalar and Einstein tensors unchanged; their
first-order coefficients depend on $h$ only through its gauge-equivalence
class.

**(f) Quadratic remainder.** For every compact $K\subseteq\Omega$ there are
$\delta_0>0$ and $C_K<\infty$ such that for every smooth symmetric component
field $A=(A_{ab})$ on a neighborhood of $K$ with

$$B_K(A):=\sup_K\max_{a,b}|A_{ab}|+L\sup_K\max_{a,b,c}|\partial_cA_{ab}|+L^2\sup_K\max_{a,b,c,d}|\partial_c\partial_dA_{ab}|\le\delta_0,$$

the metric $\eta+A$ is Lorentzian of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $K$ and

$$\Bigl|G_{ab}(\eta+A)(p)-G^{(1)}_{ab}(A)(p)\Bigr|\le \frac{C_K\,B_K(A)^2}{L^2}\qquad(p\in K),$$

where $G^{(1)}_{ab}(A)$ is the right-hand side of the displayed formula of
(c) with $h$ replaced by $A$, and $G_{ab}(\eta+A)$ is the Einstein tensor of
the metric with components $\eta_{ab}+A_{ab}$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with inertial chart $x$ and
constant metric components $\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and let
$\Omega\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set, identified with its image under
$x$; all components below are taken in the inertial chart. Let $c>0$ be a
real parameter.

**(a) Flat linearized family.** A **flat linearized family over $\Omega$**
consists of a number $\varepsilon_1>0$, a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $h$ on $\Omega$ with components $h_{ab}$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) — the **first-order
perturbation** — and a smooth family $q$ of symmetric component fields
$q_{ab}(\lambda,p)$, defined for $\lambda\in(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)$
and $p\in\Omega$, such that for every $\lambda$ with
$0<|\lambda|<\varepsilon_1$ the component field

$$g_{ab}(\lambda,p):=\eta_{ab}+\lambda\,h_{ab}(p)+\lambda^2\,q_{ab}(\lambda,p)$$

is the component field of a smooth Lorentzian metric $g(\lambda)$ on
$\Omega$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $q$ is the **normalized remainder**. The
family is thus normalized so that $g(0)=\eta$ is its value at
$\lambda=0$ and $h=\partial_\lambda g(\lambda)|_{\lambda=0}$. No assumption
is made that $g(\lambda)$ solves any field equation; the metrics $g(\lambda)$
are the mathematical input of the linearization.

**(b) First-order coefficients.** Let $A(\lambda)$ stand for any of the
component families $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(g(\lambda))$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g(\lambda))$, $S(g(\lambda))$,
$G_{ab}(g(\lambda))$ of the metric-selected connection of $g(\lambda)$; these
are smooth in $(\lambda,p)$ because the Christoffel symbols, the curvature
components and the inverse metric are smooth functions of the metric
components and their derivatives
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Define the **first-order
coefficients**

$$\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}:=\partial_\lambda\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},\quad \operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}:=\partial_\lambda\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},$$
$$S^{(1)}:=\partial_\lambda S(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}:=\partial_\lambda G_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0}.$$

**(c) Index conventions.** Indices on first-order quantities are raised and
lowered with the flat metric $\eta$ and its inverse $\eta^{ab}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]): $\partial^a:=\eta^{ab}\partial_b$,
$h^{ab}:=\eta^{ac}\eta^{bd}h_{cd}$, and

$$\Box:=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b=-\partial_0^2+\partial_1^2+\partial_2^2+\partial_3^2$$

is the **d'Alembertian** of the flat metric, applied componentwise to
component families. The **trace** of $h$ and the **trace-reversed
perturbation** are

$$h:=\eta^{ab}h_{ab},\qquad \bar h_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\tfrac12\,h\,\eta_{ab} .$$

The inverse passage is the same formula, $\bar h_{ab}$'s trace being
$\eta^{ab}\bar h_{ab}=h-2h=-h$: explicitly

$$h_{ab}=\bar h_{ab}-\tfrac12\,\eta_{ab}\,\eta^{cd}\bar h_{cd} .$$

**(d) Gauge transformation.** For a smooth covector field $\xi_b$ on
$\Omega$ define the **gauge-transformed first-order perturbation**

$$h'_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a .$$

This is the first-order perturbation of the pullback family
$\Phi_{-\lambda}^*g(\lambda)$ along the local flows $\Phi_s$ of the vector
field $\xi^a=\eta^{ab}\xi_b$, that is, the perturbation produced by the
infinitesimal chart change $x'^a=x^a+\lambda\xi^a$ and re-read on the fixed
inertial chart; the transformation of the metric components displayed here
is the linearization of the Jacobian transformation law, and
its consequences for $\bar h$ and for $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}$, $S^{(1)}$
and $G^{(1)}$ are proved separately on this page (the first-order curvature
and gauge theorem that follows this definition).
The perturbation $h$ is **in harmonic gauge** (also called de Donder gauge)
when

$$\partial^a\bar h_{ab}=0 .$$

**(e) Scope.** This item fixes the objects of the flat linearization: the
normalized family, the first-order coefficients defined as exact
$\lambda$-derivatives, the trace reversal, the d'Alembertian and the gauge
transformation. It asserts no explicit formula for the first-order
coefficients, no existence of a gauge representative satisfying (d), no
solution of any linearized field equation and no physical interpretation;
those are separate results. The notation is tied to the inertial chart: a
change of chart is a different operation from the gauge transformation (d),
which changes the metric family inside the fixed chart.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, as carried by
the cited polar-surface and divergence suppliers
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]],
[[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]]). Let
$\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on the unit sphere $S^2\subseteq
\mathbb R^3$, with $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$ as established in [F1]
([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]],
[[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]],
[[thm-volume-recursion-for-closed-euclidean-balls]],
[[thm-jordan-measurable-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable-with-equal-content]],
[[cor-volume-of-a-closed-three-ball]]), let $c>0$ be a real parameter, and
let $\Delta$ be the Laplacian of $\mathbb R^3$
([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]).

**(a) Spherical means.** For $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, signed
$r\in\mathbb R$ and $x\in\mathbb R^3$ define

$$M_rf(x):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}f(x+r\omega)\,d\sigma(\omega),\qquad H_f(x,s):=s\,M_{cs}f(x).$$

Then $Mf:(x,r)\mapsto M_rf(x)$ and $H_f$ are $C^\infty$ on
$\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$,
$M_{-r}f=M_rf$, $M_0f=f$, $\partial_x^\alpha M_rf=M_r(\partial^\alpha f)$ for every multiindex
$\alpha$, and for every $r>0$

$$r^2\,\partial_rM_rf(x)=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{B_r(x)}\Delta f(y)\,dy\quad(r>0),\qquad \partial_r^2M_rf+\frac2r\,\partial_rM_rf=\Delta M_rf\quad(r\ne0).$$

Moreover $H_f(x,0)=0$, $\partial_sH_f(x,0)=f(x)$ and
$(c^{-2}\partial_s^2-\Delta_x)H_f=0$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$.

**(b) Duhamel solution with zero data.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an
open interval, $t_0\in I$ and $F\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3\times I)$. Then

$$u(x,t):=c^2\int_{t_0}^tH_{F(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv\qquad((x,t)\in\mathbb R^3\times I)$$

is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times I$, satisfies
$u(\cdot,t_0)=0$, $\partial_tu(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and

$$(c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta_x)u=F\qquad\text{on }\mathbb R^3\times I,$$

and every partial derivative of $u$ is bounded on $K\times[a,b]$ for every
compact $K\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ and every compact interval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$.

**(c) Harmonic gauge.** Let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor
field on $\mathbb R^4$ with components $h_{ab}$ in the identity chart, let
$\bar h$ be its trace reverse and set
$F_b:=-\partial^a\bar h_{ab}\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^4)$
([[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]] clauses (b)-(c)). Then there is a
smooth covector field $\xi_b$ on $\mathbb R^4$ with
$\Box\xi_b=\partial^a\bar h_{ab}$, and for
$h'_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a$,

$$\partial^a\bar h'{}_{ab}=0,\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=-\tfrac12\,\Box\bar h'{}_{ab},$$

where $G^{(1)}$ is the first-order Einstein coefficient of
[[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]] clause (b).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $n \ge 1$
and write
$$S^{n-1}:=\{\omega \in \mathbb R^n : |\omega|=1\}.$$
Let
$$\Phi:\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\longrightarrow(0,\infty)\times S^{n-1},\qquad \Phi(x)=(|x|,x/|x|).$$
This map is continuous. If $E\subseteq S^{n-1}$ is Borel, then
$(0,1]\times E$ is Borel and
$$\{r\omega:\omega\in E,\ 0<r\le1\}=\Phi^{-1}((0,1]\times E)$$
is Borel in $\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$ by
[[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]], hence Borel in
$\mathbb R^n$ by [[thm-borel-sigma-algebra-of-a-subspace-is-the-trace]]. It is
therefore Lebesgue measurable by [[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]].
Define
$$\sigma(E):=n\,\lambda_n(\{r\omega : \omega \in E,\ 0<r\le 1\}).$$

The next theorem proves that this is a Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$ and that it
is exactly the surface measure needed for polar coordinates.

Let $n \ge 1$, **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $T : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be linear
with matrix $A$ ([[def-linear-map]],
[[lem-euclidean-linear-maps-have-matrices-and-are-bounded]]).

1. **Invertible case.** If $\det A \ne 0$, then $T[E]$ is Lebesgue measurable for
   every Lebesgue measurable $E$ and
   $$\lambda_n\big(T[E]\big) \;=\; |\det A|\;\lambda_n(E),$$
   both sides possibly $+\infty$; the product is defined in
   $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ because $|\det A| > 0$.
2. **Singular case.** If $\det A = 0$, then $T[E]$ is Lebesgue measurable with
   $\lambda_n(T[E]) = 0$ for **every** $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$.

**The singular clause is stated as nullity and not as a product.** When
$\det A = 0$ and $\lambda_n(E) = +\infty$ the expression
$|\det A|\,\lambda_n(E)$ is $0\cdot(+\infty)$, which [[def-extended-reals]]
leaves undefined; writing the conclusion as $\lambda_n(T[E]) = 0$ says the same
thing wherever the product is defined and remains a statement where it is not.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.


**(d) Intrinsic construction before physical use.** For smooth local vector
fields define the Koszul expression

$$K(X,Y,Z):=Xg(Y,Z)+Yg(Z,X)-Zg(X,Y)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X).$$

Define $\nabla^g_XY$ by $2g(\nabla^g_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)$ for every smooth local
$Z$. The proof below establishes existence, smoothness, the affine-connection
rules, metric compatibility, torsion freedom and uniqueness; it uses symmetry
and nondegeneracy, not positive definiteness. Thus $\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$
has this unique element, called the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$. The later
nondegenerate-metric theorem retains its fuller tensor-derivative statement.
Its Christoffel symbols in any chart are defined by
$\nabla^g_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]) and obey

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12 g^{ad}(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}),\qquad a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3.$$

**(e) Basic curvature and contractions.** The **curvature** of this connection
is the operator of [[def-curvature-of-an-affine-connection]], with the fixed
sign convention

$$R^g(X,Y)Z:=\nabla^g_X\nabla^g_YZ-\nabla^g_Y\nabla^g_XZ-\nabla^g_{[X,Y]}Z.$$

The general affine-connection theorem
[[thm-curvature-is-a-type-one-three-tensor]] proves that it depends pointwise
only on $X,Y,Z$ and is a smooth tensor. Define its chart components by
$R^g(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^a{}_{bcd}\partial_a$.
Define the **Ricci tensor** and **scalar curvature** pointwise by

$$\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,w):=\operatorname{tr}(z\mapsto R^g_p(z,w)v),\qquad S(p):=\operatorname{tr}(\sharp_p\circ\operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p),\qquad \operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p(v):=\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,\cdot).$$

Here $\sharp$ is the inverse metric isomorphism and traces are the
basis-independent trace of [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. Equivalently,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\sum_aR^a{}_{bad}$ and
$S=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}$, all sums from $0$ through $3$.
These are well-defined smooth fields by finite contraction of the smooth
components of $R^g$ and $g^{-1}$; basis independence follows from the trace
and the intrinsic maps just defined. No symmetry identity or field equation
is assumed here. Lowering the curvature output gives
$R_{abcd}=g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd}$, so the definitions agree with the full later
curvature item, which proves the remaining symmetries and coordinate formulas.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. That $R_{abcd}$ are the components of a smooth $(0,4)$-tensor
field and that $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth
symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field, so that the contractions above are
basis-independent and do not depend on the chart, is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clauses (a)-(d); the Ricci symmetry
is part of that statement.

Let $\Omega\subseteq M$ be an open set of the flat model
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]], let
$(\varepsilon_1,h,q)$ be a flat linearized family over $\Omega$ with
first-order coefficients $\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}$,
$\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}$, $S^{(1)}$, $G^{(1)}_{ab}$ and with trace
reversal $\bar h$, d'Alembertian $\Box$ and gauge transformation
$h'_{ab}=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a$ as in
[[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]], and let $L>0$ be a length scale.
All components are taken in the inertial chart and all contractions are
with $\eta$ and $\eta^{-1}$.

**(a) Christoffel symbols.** For every compact $K\subseteq\Omega$ there is a
constant $C_K<\infty$ such that for all $p\in K$ and
$0<|\lambda|\le\varepsilon_1/2$,

$$\Bigl|\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad \Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,\eta^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bh_{cd}+\partial_ch_{bd}-\partial_dh_{bc}\bigr).$$

**(b) Ricci tensor.** With the same constants (enlarged if necessary),

$$\Bigl|\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}=\tfrac12\bigl(\partial_c\partial_a h^{c}{}_{b}+\partial_c\partial_b h^{c}{}_{a}-\Box h_{ab}-\partial_a\partial_b h\bigr).$$

**(c) Scalar curvature and Einstein tensor.** With the same constants,

$$\Bigl|S(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,S^{(1)}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad S^{(1)}=\partial_a\partial_bh^{ab}-\Box h,$$

and

$$\Bigl|G_{ab}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,G^{(1)}_{ab}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}=-\tfrac12\,\Box\bar h_{ab}+\partial^c\partial_{(a}\bar h_{b)c}-\tfrac12\,\eta_{ab}\,\partial^c\partial^d\bar h_{cd}.$$

**(d) Gauge transformation.** For every smooth covector field $\xi$ on
$\Omega$,

$$\bar h'{}_{ab}=\bar h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a+\eta_{ab}\,\partial^c\xi_c,\qquad \partial^a\bar h'{}_{ab}=\partial^a\bar h_{ab}-\Box\xi_b .$$

Consequently $h'$ is in harmonic gauge exactly when
$\Box\xi_b=\partial^a\bar h_{ab}$, and in that case

$$G^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=-\tfrac12\,\Box\bar h'{}_{ab}.$$

**(e) Gauge invariance of the first-order curvature.** For every smooth
covector field $\xi$ on $\Omega$,

$$\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(h),\qquad S^{(1)}(h')=S^{(1)}(h),\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=G^{(1)}_{ab}(h).$$

That is, subtracting the pure-gauge perturbation
$\partial_a\xi_b+\partial_b\xi_a$ from the first-order perturbation leaves
the first-order Ricci, scalar and Einstein tensors unchanged; their
first-order coefficients depend on $h$ only through its gauge-equivalence
class.

**(f) Quadratic remainder.** For every compact $K\subseteq\Omega$ there are
$\delta_0>0$ and $C_K<\infty$ such that for every smooth symmetric component
field $A=(A_{ab})$ on a neighborhood of $K$ with

$$B_K(A):=\sup_K\max_{a,b}|A_{ab}|+L\sup_K\max_{a,b,c}|\partial_cA_{ab}|+L^2\sup_K\max_{a,b,c,d}|\partial_c\partial_dA_{ab}|\le\delta_0,$$

the metric $\eta+A$ is Lorentzian of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $K$ and

$$\Bigl|G_{ab}(\eta+A)(p)-G^{(1)}_{ab}(A)(p)\Bigr|\le \frac{C_K\,B_K(A)^2}{L^2}\qquad(p\in K),$$

where $G^{(1)}_{ab}(A)$ is the right-hand side of the displayed formula of
(c) with $h$ replaced by $A$, and $G_{ab}(\eta+A)$ is the Einstein tensor of
the metric with components $\eta_{ab}+A_{ab}$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with inertial chart $x$ and
constant metric components $\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and let
$\Omega\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set, identified with its image under
$x$; all components below are taken in the inertial chart. Let $c>0$ be a
real parameter.

**(a) Flat linearized family.** A **flat linearized family over $\Omega$**
consists of a number $\varepsilon_1>0$, a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $h$ on $\Omega$ with components $h_{ab}$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) — the **first-order
perturbation** — and a smooth family $q$ of symmetric component fields
$q_{ab}(\lambda,p)$, defined for $\lambda\in(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)$
and $p\in\Omega$, such that for every $\lambda$ with
$0<|\lambda|<\varepsilon_1$ the component field

$$g_{ab}(\lambda,p):=\eta_{ab}+\lambda\,h_{ab}(p)+\lambda^2\,q_{ab}(\lambda,p)$$

is the component field of a smooth Lorentzian metric $g(\lambda)$ on
$\Omega$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $q$ is the **normalized remainder**. The
family is thus normalized so that $g(0)=\eta$ is its value at
$\lambda=0$ and $h=\partial_\lambda g(\lambda)|_{\lambda=0}$. No assumption
is made that $g(\lambda)$ solves any field equation; the metrics $g(\lambda)$
are the mathematical input of the linearization.

**(b) First-order coefficients.** Let $A(\lambda)$ stand for any of the
component families $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(g(\lambda))$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g(\lambda))$, $S(g(\lambda))$,
$G_{ab}(g(\lambda))$ of the metric-selected connection of $g(\lambda)$; these
are smooth in $(\lambda,p)$ because the Christoffel symbols, the curvature
components and the inverse metric are smooth functions of the metric
components and their derivatives
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Define the **first-order
coefficients**

$$\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}:=\partial_\lambda\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},\quad \operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}:=\partial_\lambda\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},$$
$$S^{(1)}:=\partial_\lambda S(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}:=\partial_\lambda G_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0}.$$

**(c) Index conventions.** Indices on first-order quantities are raised and
lowered with the flat metric $\eta$ and its inverse $\eta^{ab}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]): $\partial^a:=\eta^{ab}\partial_b$,
$h^{ab}:=\eta^{ac}\eta^{bd}h_{cd}$, and

$$\Box:=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b=-\partial_0^2+\partial_1^2+\partial_2^2+\partial_3^2$$

is the **d'Alembertian** of the flat metric, applied componentwise to
component families. The **trace** of $h$ and the **trace-reversed
perturbation** are

$$h:=\eta^{ab}h_{ab},\qquad \bar h_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\tfrac12\,h\,\eta_{ab} .$$

The inverse passage is the same formula, $\bar h_{ab}$'s trace being
$\eta^{ab}\bar h_{ab}=h-2h=-h$: explicitly

$$h_{ab}=\bar h_{ab}-\tfrac12\,\eta_{ab}\,\eta^{cd}\bar h_{cd} .$$

**(d) Gauge transformation.** For a smooth covector field $\xi_b$ on
$\Omega$ define the **gauge-transformed first-order perturbation**

$$h'_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a .$$

This is the first-order perturbation of the pullback family
$\Phi_{-\lambda}^*g(\lambda)$ along the local flows $\Phi_s$ of the vector
field $\xi^a=\eta^{ab}\xi_b$, that is, the perturbation produced by the
infinitesimal chart change $x'^a=x^a+\lambda\xi^a$ and re-read on the fixed
inertial chart; the transformation of the metric components displayed here
is the linearization of the Jacobian transformation law, and
its consequences for $\bar h$ and for $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}$, $S^{(1)}$
and $G^{(1)}$ are proved separately on this page (the first-order curvature
and gauge theorem that follows this definition).
The perturbation $h$ is **in harmonic gauge** (also called de Donder gauge)
when

$$\partial^a\bar h_{ab}=0 .$$

**(e) Scope.** This item fixes the objects of the flat linearization: the
normalized family, the first-order coefficients defined as exact
$\lambda$-derivatives, the trace reversal, the d'Alembertian and the gauge
transformation. It asserts no explicit formula for the first-order
coefficients, no existence of a gauge representative satisfying (d), no
solution of any linearized field equation and no physical interpretation;
those are separate results. The notation is tied to the inertial chart: a
change of chart is a different operation from the gauge transformation (d),
which changes the metric family inside the fixed chart.

Under the hypotheses of [[thm-taylor-schlomilch-roche-remainder]], there are points $\xi_L,\xi_C$ between $a$ and $x$ such that
$$R_{n,a}f(x)=\frac{f^{(n+1)}(\xi_L)}{\iota((n+1)!)}(x-a)^{n+1}$$
and
$$R_{n,a}f(x)=\frac{f^{(n+1)}(\xi_C)}{\iota(n!)}(x-\xi_C)^n(x-a).$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), so that at every $p\in M$ the form
$g_p$ has inertia $(3,1,0)$, and let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on $M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) whose
support is compact.

**(a) Pointwise openness.** Let $V$ be a real vector space of dimension $4$
and let $G$ be a symmetric bilinear form on $V$ of inertia $(3,1,0)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]). If in some basis of $V$ the matrix of $G$
has the form $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)+E$, then $G$ has inertia $(3,1,0)$
whenever $|E_{ij}|<1/8$ for all $i,j$. Consequently, for every basis the set
of matrices of symmetric forms of inertia $(3,1,0)$ is open in the space
$M_4^{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb R)$ with respect to the maximum-entry norm, and
equivalently $g_p$ has a neighborhood in the space of symmetric forms at $p$
consisting entirely of forms of inertia $(3,1,0)$.

**(b) Global stability.** There is $\lambda_0>0$ such that for every real
$\lambda$ with $|\lambda|<\lambda_0$ the smooth symmetric field $g+\lambda h$
is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $M$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with
time orientation inherited from $N$ (the field $N$ remains timelike for
$g+\lambda h$ for $|\lambda|$ small).

derivations.claim: (The residual family.) Define $\Phi_{ab}(\lambda,p):=G_{ab}(g(\lambda))(p)+\Lambda g_{ab}(\lambda)(p)-\kappa T_{ab}(\lambda,p)$ for $(\lambda,p)\in(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)\times\Omega$. By [L1] and the smoothness of $T$, each component $\Phi_{ab}$ is differentiable in $\lambda$ at every $\lambda$. By hypothesis $\Phi_{ab}(\lambda,p)=0$ for all $(\lambda,p)$, so $\partial_\lambda\Phi_{ab}(0,p)=0$ for every $p$ (the difference quotients of the identically zero function vanish).

(Sourced wave equation.) If $h$ is in harmonic gauge and $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)+\Lambda h_{ab}=S_{ab}$, then substituting [L2] gives $-\tfrac12\Box\bar h_{ab}=S_{ab}-\Lambda h_{ab}$, that is $\Box\bar h_{ab}=2\Lambda h_{ab}-2S_{ab}$. This proves (c).

(Quadratic residual.) Let $h$ satisfy $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)=0$ on $K$ and choose $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ with $|\lambda|B_K(h)\le\delta_0=1/16$. Put $A:=\lambda h$ and at each $p\in K$ let $V_A(p)$ be the finite list $(A_{ab},\partial_cA_{ab},\partial_c\partial_dA_{ab})$. By the displayed definition of $B_K$, $\|V_A(p)\|_{\max}\le m_LB_K(A)$, where $m_L:=\max\{1,L,L^2\}$; in particular $|A_{ab}(p)|\le1/16<1/8$, so [L3] makes $\eta+A$ Lorentzian. The jet lists along all segments $tV_A(p)$, $p\in K$, $0\le t\le1$, lie in the compact set given by $\max|A_{ab}|\le1/16$, $\max|\partial_cA_{ab}|\le L\delta_0$ and $\max|\partial_c\partial_dA_{ab}|\le L^2\delta_0$. On this set the smooth Einstein-tensor map of [L3] has Hessian bounded by a finite $H_{K,L}$. Taylor's estimate along $tV_A(p)$ gives $|G_{ab}(\eta+A)(p)-G^{(1)}_{ab}(A)(p)|\le\tfrac12H_{K,L}m_L^2B_K(A)^2=C_{K,L}B_K(A)^2/L^2$, with $C_{K,L}:=\tfrac12H_{K,L}m_L^2L^2$. Since $B_K(A)=|\lambda|B_K(h)$ and $G^{(1)}_{ab}(A)=\lambda G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)=0$, this is (d).

(First-order equation.) Differentiating the definition of $\Phi$ at $\lambda=0$ and evaluating at $p$, $$0=\partial_\lambda G_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_0+\Lambda\,\partial_\lambda g_{ab}(\lambda)\big|_0-\kappa\,\left.\partial_\lambda T_{ab}(\lambda,p)\right|_{\lambda=0}.$$ By [L1] the first term is the first-order Einstein coefficient $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)(p)$, the second is $\Lambda h_{ab}(p)$, and the third is $\kappa T^{(1)}_{ab}(p)$. Hence $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)+\Lambda h_{ab}=\kappa T^{(1)}_{ab}$ on $\Omega$, which is (a).

(Vacuum branch and wave form.) If $T(\lambda)=0$ for every $\lambda$, then $T^{(1)}=0$, and with $\Lambda=0$ step 2.1 gives $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)=0$. If in addition $\partial^a\bar h_{ab}=0$, then [L2] gives $-\tfrac12\Box\bar h_{ab}=G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)=0$ for every $a,b$, so $\Box\bar h_{ab}=0$. This proves (b).

(All-space harmonic gauge.) Let $\Omega=\mathbb R^4$, let $h$ solve the linearized vacuum equations with $\Lambda=0$, and set $F_b(x,t):=-\partial^a\bar h_{ab}(x,t)$ in the coordinates $x^0=ct$. For $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ define the signed-radius mean $\widetilde M_rf(x):=(4\pi)^{-1}\int_{S^2}f(x+r\omega)\,d\sigma(\omega)$ for $r\in\mathbb R$. The integral is smooth in $(x,r)$ by differentiation under the integral on compact parameter sets, as in the proof of [[thm-gr-flat-wave-equation-duhamel-and-harmonic-gauge]] clause (a). The antipodal substitution $\omega\mapsto-\omega$ preserves $\sigma$: by the cone-volume definition in [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], the cone of $-E$ is the image of the cone of $E$ under $y\mapsto-y$, a linear map with determinant $-1$ in $\mathbb R^3$ and hence preserves Lebesgue measure by [[thm-linear-change-of-variables-for-lebesgue-measure]]. Thus $\widetilde M_{-r}f=\widetilde M_rf$, and for $r\ge0$ it agrees with $M_rf$. The kernel $\widetilde H_f(x,s):=s\widetilde M_{cs}f(x)$ is therefore smooth for signed $s$, odd in $s$, agrees with the kernel of [L2] for $s\ge0$, and satisfies $(c^{-2}\partial_s^2-\Delta_x)\widetilde H_f=0$: for $s>0$ this follows from [[thm-gr-flat-wave-equation-duhamel-and-harmonic-gauge]] clause (a), for $s<0$ by oddness, and at $s=0$ by smoothness and continuity. The same moving-endpoint differentiation as in that theorem's proof (b), now with this smooth two-sided kernel, shows that $\xi_b(x,t):=c^2\int_0^t\widetilde H_{F_b(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$ is smooth on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ and satisfies $(c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta_x)\xi_b=F_b$ for every signed $t$; hence $-\Box\xi_b=F_b=-\partial^a\bar h_{ab}$ and $\Box\xi_b=\partial^a\bar h_{ab}$. The gauge identity of [L2] then gives $\partial^a\bar h'_{ab}=0$ for $h'_{ab}=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a$. By gauge invariance in [L2] and the vacuum conclusion of step 3.1 applied only to $h$, $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)=0$; applying the harmonic-gauge identity of [L2] to $h'$ yields $\Box\bar h'_{ab}=0$. This proves (e).

(Status and conclusion.) Steps 1.1-4.1 use only the field-law hypothesis for the family, the differentiability of the component families and the cited mathematical reductions. No observation, apparatus, measured constant or statistical model is used, and the family hypothesis is precisely the adopted field law evaluated on the given families; therefore the conclusions are conditional model deductions.

boundaries.evidence: Statement and corresponding proof: Clause (d) and the Given block require K to be a nonempty compact subset of Omega, so every supremum defining B_K is a real finite number; the empty-set case is outside the stated estimate.

clause (b) and step 3.1: the source T(lambda) = 0 for every lambda gives T^{(1)} = 0 and the vacuum reduction G^{(1)} = 0; at lambda = 0 the residual of clause (d) vanishes identically, and step 1.3 covers the sourced wave equation with arbitrary S including S = 0.

boundaries.reason: No unit or rank-one normalization is asserted; Lambda, kappa and the amplitude range are arbitrary model constants, and clause (d) is stated for all |lambda| <= 1 without distinguishing the unit value.
boundaries.evidence: Statement and corresponding proof: Clause (d) holds for every real lambda satisfying |lambda|B_K(h)<=1/16; its proof uses no additional amplitude cap. L=1 is an ordinary positive scale.

statement and step 1.3: the flat linearized family is Lorentzian for |lambda| < epsilon_1, so the inverse metric and the Einstein tensor of g(lambda) exist; clause (d) additionally assumes B_K(h) <= delta_0 so that eta + lambda h stays Lorentzian on K for |lambda| <= 1.

Statement and corresponding proof: The Taylor cube includes the closed threshold |lambda|B_K(h)=1/16 with zeroth-order entries strictly below 1/8. The exact solution family is used only on its declared open interval (-epsilon1,epsilon1), and differentiation is at interior lambda=0. Signed Duhamel holds at t=0 and both time signs.

clause (e) and step 4.1 use the smooth covector field xi supplied by the all-space existence theorem, a single object; the proof selects no family of sets or points, and the only choice principle is the inherited countable choice of the cited suppliers.

boundaries.reason: The theorem states a derivation of the linearized equation and its reductions, not an equivalence.

The field law is differentiated in clause (a); vacuum and gauge hypotheses yield clauses (b)–(c), and clause (e) supplies a harmonic-gauge transform on all space. These conditional reductions do not claim that a linearized solution integrates to an exact sourced model family.
