citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)=(\mathbb R^4,\eta,\partial_0)$ be the flat model with its
inertial chart $x$ and metric components
$\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$
([[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Since the chart identifies each
$T_p\mathbb R^4$ with $\mathbb R^4$, all objects below are defined by their
components in this chart; they are the components at a point, and a subscript
$p$ is suppressed. Indices are raised and lowered with $\eta$ and $\eta^{-1}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]), and orthogonality is in
the sense of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]].

**(a) Observer, propagation direction, screen.** Let $n=n^a\partial_a$ be an
**observer** of the flat model: $n$ is future-directed, $\eta(n,n)=-1$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]); and let
$s=s^a\partial_a$ be a **propagation direction**: $\eta(s,s)=1$ and
$\eta(n,s)=0$. The pair defines the two-dimensional **screen**
$\Sigma(n,s):=\{v\in\mathbb R^4:\eta(v,n)=0,\ \eta(v,s)=0\}$, on which the
restriction of $\eta$ is positive definite by
[[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]. The **screen projector** and
the **spatial projector** of the pair are the $(1,1)$-tensors with components

$$p^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b-s^as_b,\qquad h^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b,$$

and the covariant form of the screen projector is
$p_{ab}:=\eta_{ac}p^c{}_b=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b-s_as_b$. The properties $p^2=p$,
$h^2=h$, $\operatorname{im}p=\Sigma(n,s)$ and $\operatorname{im}h=n^\perp$
are proved in the screen-projector lemma of this page.

**(b) TT projection.** Let $A=(A_{ab})$ be a symmetric covariant $2$-tensor
at a point. Its **transverse-traceless (TT) projection with respect to
$(n,s)$** is the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor

$$\Pi_{n,s}(A)_{ab}:=p_a{}^cp_b{}^dA_{cd}-\tfrac12\,p_{ab}\,p^{cd}A_{cd},\qquad p^{cd}:=\eta^{ce}\eta^{df}p_{ef}.$$

**(c) Screen amplitudes.** Let $(e_1,e_2)$ be an ordered
$\eta$-orthonormal basis of $\Sigma(n,s)$ (which exists by
[[cor-finite-dimensional-inner-product-spaces-have-orthonormal-bases]] applied
to the positive-definite restriction of $\eta$). For a symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor $A$ the **plus and cross amplitudes of $A$ with respect to
$(e_1,e_2)$** are $A_+:=A(e_1,e_1)$ and $A_\times:=A(e_1,e_2)$; if $A$ is
TT with respect to $(n,s)$ in the sense of clause (d) below, then in the dual
basis $(e^1,e^2)$ of the screen

$$A=A_+\bigl(e^1\otimes e^1-e^2\otimes e^2\bigr)+A_\times\bigl(e^1\otimes e^2+e^2\otimes e^1\bigr).$$

For a TT screen tensor $A$, under the rotation
$e_1'=\cos\theta\,e_1+\sin\theta\,e_2$,
$e_2'=-\sin\theta\,e_1+\cos\theta\,e_2$ of the screen basis the amplitudes
transform as $A_+'=A_+\cos2\theta+A_\times\sin2\theta$ and
$A_\times'=-A_+\sin2\theta+A_\times\cos2\theta$. Here $\sin$ and $\cos$
are the power-series functions of [[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]];
expanding $A(e_1',e_1')$ and $A(e_1',e_2')$ by bilinearity and applying the
addition formulas of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]] gives the two
displayed transformations.

**(d) TT tensors and TT perturbations.** A symmetric covariant $2$-tensor
$A$ is **transverse-traceless (TT) with respect to $(n,s)$** when
$A(n,\cdot)=0$, $A(s,\cdot)=0$ and $\eta^{ab}A_{ab}=0$. For a symmetric
field $h$ on an open set of the flat model, "TT with respect to $(n,s)$"
means that these three conditions hold at every point. A symmetric field $h$
is **spatial with respect to $n$** when $h(n,\cdot)=0$ at every point.

**(e) Scope.** This item fixes the screen, the two projections and the
amplitude terminology, and states the rotation law of clause (c) as part of
the naming. It asserts no property of $\Pi_{n,s}$ (idempotence, rank, image
and trace are proved in the screen-projector lemma of this page), no relation
to the planar perturbations of the plane-wave definition of this page
(established in the gauge-decomposition lemma of this page) and no physical
interpretation of the amplitudes.

Let $(M,g,N)=(\mathbb R^4,\eta,\partial_0)$ be the flat model with its
inertial chart ([[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]]), let $(n,s)$
be an observer and propagation direction and let $p$, $h$, $\Sigma(n,s)$,
$\Pi_{n,s}$ and the amplitude terminology be as in
[[def-gr-wave-screen-and-tt-projection]]. Write $V:=\mathbb R^4$ and let
$\mathcal S$ be the space of symmetric covariant $2$-tensors on $V$. Then:

**(a) Projections.** $p$ and $h$ are linear endomorphisms of $V$ with
$p^2=p$, $h^2=h$, $\ker p=\operatorname{span}\{n,s\}$,
$\operatorname{im}p=\Sigma(n,s)$, $\ker h=\mathbb Rn$,
$\operatorname{im}h=n^\perp$; both are $\eta$-self-adjoint,
$\eta(pu,v)=\eta(u,pv)$ and $\eta(hu,v)=\eta(u,hv)$ for all $u,v$. Moreover
$h-p=s^\flat\otimes s$, that is $h^a{}_b-p^a{}_b=s^as_b$.

**(b) Ranks and traces.** $\operatorname{rank}p=\dim\Sigma(n,s)=2$,
$p^a{}_a=2$, $\operatorname{rank}h=3$, $h^a{}_a=3$.

**(c) TT projection.** $\Pi_{n,s}$ is a linear endomorphism of $\mathcal S$
with $\Pi_{n,s}^2=\Pi_{n,s}$; for every $A\in\mathcal S$ the tensor
$\Pi_{n,s}(A)$ is TT with respect to $(n,s)$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-wave-screen-and-tt-projection]] clause (d); and $\Pi_{n,s}(A)=A$
exactly when $A$ is TT. The TT tensors form the two-dimensional linear
subspace $T_{n,s}=\{B\in\mathcal S:B(n,\cdot)=B(s,\cdot)=0,\ \eta^{ab}B_{ab}=0\}$,
so $\dim T_{n,s}=2$.

**(d) Orthogonal projection and amplitudes.** Let
$\langle A,B\rangle:=h^{ac}h^{bd}A_{ab}B_{cd}$ on the subspace of tensors
spatial with respect to $n$. This is a positive definite inner product, and
for every spatial $A$ and every TT $B$, $\langle A-\Pi_{n,s}(A),B\rangle=0$;
so $\Pi_{n,s}$ restricted to the spatial tensors is the orthogonal projection
onto $T_{n,s}$ ([[def-orthogonal-projection]],
[[thm-finite-dimensional-orthogonal-decomposition]]). With respect to an
ordered $\eta$-orthonormal screen basis $(e_1,e_2)$ a TT tensor is

$$B=B_{11}\bigl(e^1\otimes e^1-e^2\otimes e^2\bigr)+B_{12}\bigl(e^1\otimes e^2+e^2\otimes e^1\bigr),$$

so $B$ is determined by the pair $(A_+,A_\times)=(B_{11},B_{12})$, and under
a screen rotation by $\theta$ this pair transforms as in
[[def-gr-wave-screen-and-tt-projection]] clause (c); in particular the map
$T_{n,s}\to\mathbb R^2$, $B\mapsto(A_+,A_\times)$, is a linear isomorphism.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(a) Observers.** An **observer at $p$** is a tangent vector
$n\in T_pM$ such that $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ is future-directed in the sense of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], that is, $g_p(n,N_p)<0$. Because
$g_p(n,n)=-1\neq0$, an observer is timelike and in particular nonzero
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). Observers at $p$ exist:
the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and
$n:=N_p/\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}$ satisfies $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and
$g_p(n,N_p)=-\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}<0$, where the square root is the
nonnegative root of [[def-rational-power]]; then $-n$ is a unit timelike
vector with $g_p(-n,N_p)>0$, so it is not an observer, and the two vectors
$n,-n$ point in opposite time directions.

**(b) Rest space.** For an observer $n$ at $p$, the **rest space** of $n$ is
the $g_p$-orthogonal complement of the line $\mathbb Rn$,

$$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM: g_p(v,n)=0\},$$

in the sense of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. It is
a linear subspace of $T_pM$. The further facts that $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and
that the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive definite are proved
in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]; they are consequences, not
part of the definition.

**(c) Spatial projection.** The **spatial projection** of the observer $n$ is
the map

$$h_n:T_pM\longrightarrow T_pM,\qquad h_n(v):=v+g_p(n,v)\,n .$$

The map is linear because $g_p$ is bilinear, its image is contained in
$n^{\perp}$, and it fixes $n^{\perp}$ pointwise; that it is the
$g_p$-orthogonal projection onto $n^{\perp}$ with kernel $\mathbb Rn$ is
proved in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]].

**(d) Scope.** An observer at $p$ is a single tangent vector. It is not an
ordered basis or frame of $T_pM$, not a chart, not a field of observers such as
the congruences defined later on this page, and not a curve or a worldline: no
parametrized curve, clock reading, proper time or measurement is attached to
$n$ by this definition. The physical reading of an observer as the direction
of an ideal clock's worldline, and the measurement interpretation of the
observer-relative quantities introduced later on this page, belong to the
physical postulates and unit conventions of the framework and are not asserted
here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b,\qquad g_{ac}(q)g^{cb}(q)=\delta_a{}^b,$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

Let $(M,g,N)=(\mathbb R^4,\eta,\partial_0)$ be the flat model with its
inertial chart ([[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]]), let $(n,s)$
be an observer and propagation direction and let $p$, $h$, $\Sigma(n,s)$,
$\Pi_{n,s}$ and the amplitude terminology be as in
[[def-gr-wave-screen-and-tt-projection]]. Write $V:=\mathbb R^4$ and let
$\mathcal S$ be the space of symmetric covariant $2$-tensors on $V$. Then:

**(a) Projections.** $p$ and $h$ are linear endomorphisms of $V$ with
$p^2=p$, $h^2=h$, $\ker p=\operatorname{span}\{n,s\}$,
$\operatorname{im}p=\Sigma(n,s)$, $\ker h=\mathbb Rn$,
$\operatorname{im}h=n^\perp$; both are $\eta$-self-adjoint,
$\eta(pu,v)=\eta(u,pv)$ and $\eta(hu,v)=\eta(u,hv)$ for all $u,v$. Moreover
$h-p=s^\flat\otimes s$, that is $h^a{}_b-p^a{}_b=s^as_b$.

**(b) Ranks and traces.** $\operatorname{rank}p=\dim\Sigma(n,s)=2$,
$p^a{}_a=2$, $\operatorname{rank}h=3$, $h^a{}_a=3$.

**(c) TT projection.** $\Pi_{n,s}$ is a linear endomorphism of $\mathcal S$
with $\Pi_{n,s}^2=\Pi_{n,s}$; for every $A\in\mathcal S$ the tensor
$\Pi_{n,s}(A)$ is TT with respect to $(n,s)$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-wave-screen-and-tt-projection]] clause (d); and $\Pi_{n,s}(A)=A$
exactly when $A$ is TT. The TT tensors form the two-dimensional linear
subspace $T_{n,s}=\{B\in\mathcal S:B(n,\cdot)=B(s,\cdot)=0,\ \eta^{ab}B_{ab}=0\}$,
so $\dim T_{n,s}=2$.

**(d) Orthogonal projection and amplitudes.** Let
$\langle A,B\rangle:=h^{ac}h^{bd}A_{ab}B_{cd}$ on the subspace of tensors
spatial with respect to $n$. This is a positive definite inner product, and
for every spatial $A$ and every TT $B$, $\langle A-\Pi_{n,s}(A),B\rangle=0$;
so $\Pi_{n,s}$ restricted to the spatial tensors is the orthogonal projection
onto $T_{n,s}$ ([[def-orthogonal-projection]],
[[thm-finite-dimensional-orthogonal-decomposition]]). With respect to an
ordered $\eta$-orthonormal screen basis $(e_1,e_2)$ a TT tensor is

$$B=B_{11}\bigl(e^1\otimes e^1-e^2\otimes e^2\bigr)+B_{12}\bigl(e^1\otimes e^2+e^2\otimes e^1\bigr),$$

so $B$ is determined by the pair $(A_+,A_\times)=(B_{11},B_{12})$, and under
a screen rotation by $\theta$ this pair transforms as in
[[def-gr-wave-screen-and-tt-projection]] clause (c); in particular the map
$T_{n,s}\to\mathbb R^2$, $B\mapsto(A_+,A_\times)$, is a linear isomorphism.

Let $(M,g,N)=(\mathbb R^4,\eta,\partial_0)$ be the flat model with its
inertial chart $x$ and metric components
$\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$
([[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Since the chart identifies each
$T_p\mathbb R^4$ with $\mathbb R^4$, all objects below are defined by their
components in this chart; they are the components at a point, and a subscript
$p$ is suppressed. Indices are raised and lowered with $\eta$ and $\eta^{-1}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]), and orthogonality is in
the sense of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]].

**(a) Observer, propagation direction, screen.** Let $n=n^a\partial_a$ be an
**observer** of the flat model: $n$ is future-directed, $\eta(n,n)=-1$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]); and let
$s=s^a\partial_a$ be a **propagation direction**: $\eta(s,s)=1$ and
$\eta(n,s)=0$. The pair defines the two-dimensional **screen**
$\Sigma(n,s):=\{v\in\mathbb R^4:\eta(v,n)=0,\ \eta(v,s)=0\}$, on which the
restriction of $\eta$ is positive definite by
[[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]. The **screen projector** and
the **spatial projector** of the pair are the $(1,1)$-tensors with components

$$p^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b-s^as_b,\qquad h^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b,$$

and the covariant form of the screen projector is
$p_{ab}:=\eta_{ac}p^c{}_b=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b-s_as_b$. The properties $p^2=p$,
$h^2=h$, $\operatorname{im}p=\Sigma(n,s)$ and $\operatorname{im}h=n^\perp$
are proved in the screen-projector lemma of this page.

**(b) TT projection.** Let $A=(A_{ab})$ be a symmetric covariant $2$-tensor
at a point. Its **transverse-traceless (TT) projection with respect to
$(n,s)$** is the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor

$$\Pi_{n,s}(A)_{ab}:=p_a{}^cp_b{}^dA_{cd}-\tfrac12\,p_{ab}\,p^{cd}A_{cd},\qquad p^{cd}:=\eta^{ce}\eta^{df}p_{ef}.$$

**(c) Screen amplitudes.** Let $(e_1,e_2)$ be an ordered
$\eta$-orthonormal basis of $\Sigma(n,s)$ (which exists by
[[cor-finite-dimensional-inner-product-spaces-have-orthonormal-bases]] applied
to the positive-definite restriction of $\eta$). For a symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor $A$ the **plus and cross amplitudes of $A$ with respect to
$(e_1,e_2)$** are $A_+:=A(e_1,e_1)$ and $A_\times:=A(e_1,e_2)$; if $A$ is
TT with respect to $(n,s)$ in the sense of clause (d) below, then in the dual
basis $(e^1,e^2)$ of the screen

$$A=A_+\bigl(e^1\otimes e^1-e^2\otimes e^2\bigr)+A_\times\bigl(e^1\otimes e^2+e^2\otimes e^1\bigr).$$

For a TT screen tensor $A$, under the rotation
$e_1'=\cos\theta\,e_1+\sin\theta\,e_2$,
$e_2'=-\sin\theta\,e_1+\cos\theta\,e_2$ of the screen basis the amplitudes
transform as $A_+'=A_+\cos2\theta+A_\times\sin2\theta$ and
$A_\times'=-A_+\sin2\theta+A_\times\cos2\theta$. Here $\sin$ and $\cos$
are the power-series functions of [[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]];
expanding $A(e_1',e_1')$ and $A(e_1',e_2')$ by bilinearity and applying the
addition formulas of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]] gives the two
displayed transformations.

**(d) TT tensors and TT perturbations.** A symmetric covariant $2$-tensor
$A$ is **transverse-traceless (TT) with respect to $(n,s)$** when
$A(n,\cdot)=0$, $A(s,\cdot)=0$ and $\eta^{ab}A_{ab}=0$. For a symmetric
field $h$ on an open set of the flat model, "TT with respect to $(n,s)$"
means that these three conditions hold at every point. A symmetric field $h$
is **spatial with respect to $n$** when $h(n,\cdot)=0$ at every point.

**(e) Scope.** This item fixes the screen, the two projections and the
amplitude terminology, and states the rotation law of clause (c) as part of
the naming. It asserts no property of $\Pi_{n,s}$ (idempotence, rank, image
and trace are proved in the screen-projector lemma of this page), no relation
to the planar perturbations of the plane-wave definition of this page
(established in the gauge-decomposition lemma of this page) and no physical
interpretation of the amplitudes.

derivations.claim: (The "half-trace" tensor.) By [L1], $h_a{}^ch_b{}^dA_{cd}=A$ because $A$ is spatial, and $h^{cd}A_{cd}=A_{11}+A_{22}+A_{33}=1+1+0=2$; hence $$A^{\mathrm{TT}}=A-\tfrac12\cdot2\,h=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,1,0)-\operatorname{diag}(0,1,1,1)=\operatorname{diag}(0,0,0,-1).$$

(Failure of trace-freeness and the rank-two contrast.) The tensor $A^{\mathrm{TT}}=\operatorname{diag}(0,0,0,-1)$ kills $n=\partial_0$, but $A^{\mathrm{TT}}(s,s)=-1$ for $s=\partial_3$, so it is not propagation-transverse; its trace is $\eta^{ab}A^{\mathrm{TT}}_{ab}=\eta^{33}(-1)=-1\ne0$, so the asserted conclusion fails. By contrast, [L2] computes that the same half-trace formula with the rank-two screen projector gives $\Pi_{n,s}(A)=0$, which is trace-free: the failure is exactly the rank-three projector weight. This refutes the statement.

boundaries.reason: The counterexample exhibits one explicit symmetric tensor A = diag(0,1,1,0) with A(n,.) = 0; no family, index set or empty sum is quantified and the flat model is the nonempty space R^4.

boundaries.evidence: step 2.1: the displayed trace is eta^{ab} A^{TT}_{ab} = -1 != 0, so the failure is quantitative; the zero tensor would give A^{TT} = 0 and is fixed by the formula, and the worked A satisfies A(n,.) = 0 as the refuted statement requires.

boundaries.reason: No unit normalization or single-element case is asserted; the tensor A is the rank-two screen projector of the pair (n,s) as a chosen instance, and its rank is a computed property rather than a normalization.

boundaries.evidence: Statement and corresponding proof: steps 1.1 and 2.1: the rank-three spatial projector h fixes every spatial tensor while the rank-two screen projector p projects onto the screen; the trace of the half-trace tensor with h is -1 != 0, whereas the same formula with p gives the vanishing projection of the remark, so the failure is exactly the projector weight and not a degenerate tensor case.

boundaries.reason: The computation is a finite-dimensional matrix identity at one point of the flat model; no interval, parameter endpoint or limiting process is involved.

boundaries.evidence: Statement and corresponding proof: the counterexample works in the one adapted basis and performs explicit matrix arithmetic; it selects no family and no choice principle beyond the inherited countable choice of the cited suppliers.
